'''''Sedum multiceps''''', also known as '''miniature/pygmy Joshua tree''', is a [[perennial plant|perennial]], [[deciduous]] species of ''[[Sedum]]'' from the [[succulent plant]] family [[Crassulaceae]], native to Algeria.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=33520|title=Taxon: Sedum multiceps Coss. & Durieu|author=(([[United States Department of Agriculture|USDA]], [[Agricultural Research Service]], [[National Plant Germplasm System]])) |publisher=[[Germplasm Resources Information Network]]|year=2018|accessdate=June 8, 2018}}</ref> The plant is nicknamed for its glaucous leaves that grow in clusters, resembling ''[[Yucca brevifolia]]''. It was named officially as a distinct species in 1862.

==Description==
''Sedum multiceps'' has a many-branched, shrubby [[habit (biology)#Structure|habit]], and consists of grayish-green leaves growing at the tips of its branches. It grows shallow roots and mats of short [[woody plant|woody]] stems which spread rapidly across large areas, and sprouts bright yellow, star-shaped flowers in late summer.<ref>{{cite book|title=The European Garden Flora Flowering Plants: A Manual for the Identification of Plants Cultivated in Europe, Both Out-of-Doors and Under Glass|editor1-last=Cullen|editor1-first=James|editor2-last=Knees|editor2-first=Sabrina G.|editor3-last=Cubey|editor3-first=H. Suzanne|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2011|isbn=9780521761512}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Sedum multiceps'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], typically for planting in containers or in gardens as [[groundcover]]. It needs very little attention, and tolerates all but the most loamy soil.
